<task id="ses_f2b27094effegSmeOItg5cTU6c" state="completed">
<task_result>
- Settings is roomier and easier to scan: sections are grouped with icons in the sidebar, each page has a clear title, and every setting sits on its own row with its switch or button on the right.
- OpenCode workers keep working when OpenCode 2 has taken over the `opencode` command: they find your OpenCode 1 install, and if there isn't one, the task stops straight away and says what to do instead of failing with an unrecognized flag. A worker can also point at a specific OpenCode 1 install.
- OpenCode 2 workers work again with OpenCode 2.0 and later, even when that install has also taken over the `opencode` command. Tasks, follow-ups, the model list with its effort levels, and continuing a task in a terminal all work, and a worker can point at a specific OpenCode 2 install.
- Picking a task from the list now puts you straight in its reply box.
- ⌘B (Ctrl+B on Windows and Linux) now shows or hides the task list, and puts you right in it so the arrow keys move between tasks.
- The reply box is simpler: task details and options now live behind the + button, so typing your next message is the only thing in the way.
- Settings can now pick the worker for you: turn on Choosing a worker, paste your TypeSafe key, and work you hand over without naming a worker lands on the one whose strengths fit what you asked for. Your own rules still catch anything it can't answer, and the task shows which worker was suggested and whether the work went there.
- Claude workers can now run newer models, like Opus 5.5, by using the Claude Code already installed on your machine instead of the older copy Oga shipped with.
- A task no longer fails with a confusing error when it starts just as Oga itself is starting up.
- The reply box no longer jumps when the note about continuing a paused task appears, and that note now lines up with the options under the box.
- Text in a task's activity log — command output, labels, and the response — now reads at one consistent size instead of jumping between sizes.
</task_result>
</task>

content.text:
## TL;DR
- Three read-only surveys completed: Rust crates, activity-domain files, and unreleased changelog notes.
- All three subagents ran in parallel using the native `Task` tool.

### A. Rust crates
- `oga-acp` — Integrates with the Agent Client Protocol and runs agent sessions.
- `oga-advisor` — Makes requests to an advisor service.
- `oga-client` — Provides a client for calling Oga APIs.
- `oga-config` — Defines and loads application configuration.
- `oga-context` — Builds searchable code context using parsers for multiple languages.
- `oga-domain` — Holds shared domain types and data models.
- `oga-events` — Handles application events and event storage.
- `oga-http` — Provides the HTTP API.
- `oga-mcp` — Provides the MCP server and tools.
- `oga-pricing` — Fetches and manages pricing data.
- `oga-providers` — Defines integrations with agent providers.
- `oga-routing` — Loads and applies routing rules.
- `oga-runner` — Runs provider processes and manages their I/O.
- `oga-service` — Coordinates application services and workflows.
- `oga-store` — Provides SQLite-backed persistence.
- `oga-worktree` — Manages Git worktrees and related operations.

### B. Activity domain
- `index.ts` — Exports `ActivityStory`, `ActivityStoryProjection`, activity and handoff types, composition and duration helpers, event normalization helpers, and activity constants.
- `acp.test.ts` — Tests streamed ACP activity rows; no main exports.
- `index.test.ts` — Tests activity composition; no main exports.
- `fixtures/` — Sample JSON and JSONL files: `claude-acp-resumed.json`, `probe-rows.json`, `antigravity-acp-probe.json`, and `antigravity-run.jsonl`.

### C. Unreleased changelog
- Settings is roomier and easier to scan, with grouped sections, clear page titles, and settings arranged in rows.
- OpenCode workers can find an OpenCode 1 install when OpenCode 2 has taken over `opencode`, or stop with guidance if none exists; workers can also target a specific install.
- OpenCode 2 workers work with OpenCode 2.0 and later, including tasks, follow-ups, model effort levels, terminal continuation, and specific-install selection.
- Selecting a task opens its reply box.
- ⌘B (Ctrl+B on Windows and Linux) toggles the task list and focuses it for keyboard navigation.
- Task details and options are behind the reply box’s + button.
- Settings can suggest a worker based on a TypeSafe key and show whether the suggestion was used.
- Claude workers can use newer models through the installed Claude Code.
- Tasks no longer fail with a confusing error when started as Oga starts.
- The reply box no longer jumps when the paused-task continuation note appears; the note aligns with its options.
- Activity-log text now uses a consistent size.
